name: @browzer/skills
description: AI agent skills to empower your workflow with Browzer — hybrid vector + Graph RAG for codebases and document workspaces. Skills around the `browzer` CLI: RAG search, dependency graph, doc ingestion, workspace management, and an end-to-end dev pipeline (brainstorming → generate-prd → scope-feature → generate-task → execute-task → write-tests → code-review → receiving-code-review → feature-acceptance → finalize-feature → commit). Code-review spawns 4 mandatory parallel agents (senior-engineer, software-architect, qa, regression-tester); the regression-tester lane runs the canonical pre-push gate at PACKAGE granularity, enumerates failures per-test, and reproduces each against `main` via git stash before marking `preExistingOnMain`. Receiving-code-review closes EVERY finding with a 7-step ladder for zero-tech-debt by default. Write-tests authors green coverage AND runs Stryker/mutmut/go-mutesting in the same pass; Phase 1.0 pre-flight probes test infra before declaring 'no setup'. Feature-acceptance Phase 1.5 live-verifies before deferring manual-AC items, with a metric anti-soft-override regex that blocks autonomous flips of perception metrics to `resolved:true` without operator reply. Finalize-feature absorbs both host-doc patching (Phase A, inline browzer discovery; smart-skip when no exported-symbol drift) and the committed README render (Phase B). Orchestrate-task-delivery routes brainstorming-when-needed at Step 0, then drives the autonomous chain via an explicit loop in the skill body; execute-task internally resolves serial / parallel / parallel-worktrees / agent-teams strategy with a capability probe. Universal subagent preamble requires `browzer deps --reverse` blast-radius probing before edits.
